content.text: I’ve reviewed all 4,050 candidates. The latest observations show that several predicted enantiomer gaps reversed, while IPA sensitivity persisted in both alcohol enantiomers. I’m using those results to balance targeted transfer tests, matched controls, and broader chemical coverage in the 32 selections.

  "feedback_interpretation": "Historical errors show substitution-specific transfer failures: ortho-methoxy nitro and later silicon probes reversed earlier residual directions. Several predicted stereochemical gaps reversed or collapsed, while stronger-than-predicted IPA sensitivity persisted in both alcohol enantiomers. Sulfonyl pyrrolidine residuals were mixed. These frozen historical errors are not current-candidate errors. Centers are MSE-trained predictions, not medians; widths are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and coverage is nearest-labeled raw-gradient distance percentile. Relative contrasts and matching residual signs do not establish chemical mechanisms.",
  "batch_rationale": "All 4,050 candidates were considered globally. The batch combines observed-neighbor completions, a clean IPA contrast, four thioether fluorination controls, matched homologs, and chemically distinct coverage extensions. Acid-ester and cyclopentenone comparisons isolate useful chemical changes; the amide supplies contextual coverage at different IPA. Selection avoids redundant identical-condition experiments and balances long-retention learning with direct low-center tests. No page, scaffold, stereochemistry, or condition quotas were imposed.",

    "How does fluorinated imidazole-ketone retention vary between short alkyl, longer alkyl, and phenyl side chains?",
    "Is the large predicted benzodioxane acid-ester contrast measured at fixed conditions?",
    "Do bromo and ortho-chloro sulfonyl pyrrolidines have larger stereochemical gaps than their para-fluoro and para-chloro counterparts?",
    "Do near-zero enol ester centers represent genuine short retention or a local prediction failure?",
